simple.meaning: עִזָּבוֹן (ʻizzâbôwn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “trade , i.e. the place (mart) or the payment (revenue).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 27:12. Its contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עִזָּבוֹן (H5801).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: trade , i.e. the place (mart) or the payment (revenue)
definitions.full: H5801. izzabon [ עִזָּבוֺן ] noun [masculine] only plural wares (as left in the purchaser's hand; compare Assyrian uzub(b)u , a specific payment ); — suffix 2 feminine singular עִזְּבוֺנַיִךְ Ezek 27:27 , 33 , נָ֑יִךְ - 27:12 4 t.; — wares , only Ezekiel 27 (often || מַעֲרָב q. v. below ערב ); ע נָָֽתְנוּ וְעוֺפֶרֶת בְּדִיל ׳בַּרְזֶל 27:12 iron, tin and lead they furnished as thy wares ; similarly 27:14 ; 27:22 ; also 27:16 ( ׳בְּע ᵑ0 , but probably del בְּ ); ׳בְּע נָָֽתְנוּ 27:19 at the price of ( in exchange for ) thy wares they furnished , etc.; וְע ׳הוֺנֵךְ (as subject of sentence) 27:27 ; ׳ע מִיַּמִּים בְּצֵאת 27:33 when thy wares came forth , etc.
definitions.rootNote: from 5800 in the sense of letting go (for a price, i.e. selling);

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘ “Tarshish was your merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches. They traded for your wares with silver, iron, tin, and lead.
“ ‘ “They of the house of Togarmah traded for your wares with horses, war horses, and mules.
“ ‘ “Syria was your merchant by reason of the multitude of your handiworks. They traded for your wares with emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
“ ‘ “Vedan and Javan traded with yarn for your wares: bright iron, cassia, and calamus were among your merchandise.
“ ‘ “The traders of Sheba and Raamah were your traders. They traded for your wares with the chief of all spices, and with all precious stones, and gold.
